method: Static reverse engineering of each original artifact; no sample was executed. Scans and reputation were leads, not verdict evidence.

samples.identification: NanoCoreFinal-labelled .NET surveillance and ransomware hybrid; the label does not establish authentic NanoCore lineage
evidence: CLR entry point MethodDef 57 (Main, RVA 0x2908) installs plugins and starts clipboard, screenshot, file collection, reverse shell, command executor, replication and impact workers.
KeyloggerModule.Start installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL=13. HookCallback records key events and foreground-window context; SendLoop appends the buffer to a WindowsUpdate-disguised keylog file every 30 seconds.

Main launches account creation, logon-task persistence, Defender-disable and fodhelper DelegateExecute commands. DeleteShadowCopies (RVA 0x494c) launches vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet and wmic shadowcopy delete.
The reverse-shell worker obtains a TcpClient stream, starts cmd.exe with redirected standard streams and creates paired socket-to-stdin and stdout-to-socket relay workers.

RealEncryption's worker (RVA 0x4718) enumerates Desktop/TestFolder recursively, attempts AES encryption, writes a suffixed file and deletes the input. The AES key string is 17 bytes and the IV is 14 bytes; setting the invalid key fails before encryption, output or deletion. Existing detection correctly says attempted replacement.

SendToC2 (RVA 0x42b4) XORs UTF-8 records with byte key i XOR 0xaa, Base64-encodes them, then builds an HTTP GET. C2_DOMAIN already contains http:// and is prefixed with http:// again; the TCP connector is also passed a URL instead of a hostname. Successful exfiltration or remote control is not established.

ProcessHollowing actually allocates memory and starts a remote thread in notepad; it does not hollow an image. The AMSI_Patch and ETW_Patch technique labels are only records passed to SendToC2; they do not implement those patches. Existing firing traits do not assert these unsupported mechanisms.
samples.trait_disposition: Retain accurate existing recording, attack-command and attempt detections; no sample-specific change.

samples.identification: SciTE-disguised AutoIt RunPE loader carrying njRAT 0.7d
evidence: PE resource SCRIPT_DATUM is an AU3 EA06 container. Parsing its bytes after the 24-byte header yields a tokenized script; the usual extractor misses the renamed resource.

The script conceals API strings as pipe-separated decimal character codes and flattens control flow into numeric Switch states. Following state assignments recovers the actual execution order and distinguishes junk assignments and GUI branches.

Y3235YFQ reads its own file and splits the resource container on its Netseal delimiter. Fields select encrypted payload, key, host image, startup mode 2 and watchdog mode 1. The resource's cvtres path is rewritten to RegAsm before activation.
R3231YPYIK writes an HKCU CurrentVersion/Run value and copies itself into common AppData with hidden/system attributes. R3238KGBJ decrypts the payload and passes those bytes to K3333TZQT.

K3333TZQT calls CreateProcessW with CREATE_SUSPENDED, obtains thread context, maps PE headers/sections into remote memory, updates the image base and entry context, and calls SetThreadContext and ResumeThread.

CryptDeriveKey uses CALG_RC4 and CALG_MD5. Independently deriving MD5 of the configured key and RC4-decrypting resource field 1 recovers a 24064-byte managed PE. The same process recovers a music-list password decoy from field 6.

The recovered managed PE has namespace j, OK/kl classes, version 0.7d and njRAT's command framing. Entry A.main calls OK.ko, which starts the RC receive worker and kl.WRK polling keylogger. TCP input reaches OK.Ind, which handles downloaded execution and reflective plugin activation; kl.WRK records GetAsyncKeyState input and window context in registry-backed logs.
WinInet and BlockInput imports belong to the AutoIt interpreter's built-in API support. They do not prove HTTP staging or input lockdown by this script.
samples.trait_disposition: Remove autoit-scite-wininet-spyware-control; preserve the supported masquerade, RunPE and startup-copy detections.

samples.identification: Statically linked i386 Mirai bot with router propagation and multiple packet-flood handlers
evidence: ELF entry reaches main at 0x080514f0; main daemonizes and launches process-control, scanner and attack workers. The bot parser at 0x08048250 converts received task bytes into target/option arrays and dispatches through the attack-handler table initialized at 0x080485b0.

Scanner worker 0x08053710 retries credential pairs on remote sockets, recognizes login prompts, enters router CLI shells, sends ping ;sh and BusyBox transfer commands, and runs chmod +x .d; ./.d. These are transmitted commands, not unused strings.

The UDP attack handler at 0x08048a30 constructs IPv4/UDP headers, mutates target addresses and checksums, repeatedly sends packets, advances the target by 24 bytes and branches back. Call 0x08048fe3 reaches 0x08057b10, which packs six sendto arguments and passes socketcall subcommand 11 to 0x0805980b's int 0x80 syscall 102.
RC4-style transforms at 0x08050970 and 0x080558d0 use the compact GET/dlr. token and a 256-byte key table respectively. GET/dlr. in the first transform is key material, not by itself an HTTP request.

Decoding the embedded backslash-x shell argument recovers a /proc/PID/exe readlink loop. It selects the Linux space-plus-(deleted) suffix, strips that suffix, excludes a few init/systemd paths and issues kill -9 against the selected PIDs. Selection is not restricted to competing bots.
samples.trait_disposition: Add a decoded suffix-to-SIGKILL matcher and a bound i386 send-loop detector. Place the deleted-image impact composites under degrade/process rather than rival-bot. Preserve existing family and propagation detections.

placement_review.reason: A deleted-image suffix selects processes, not a named rival. Existing hex matchers and scopes remain intact; decoded layout support is a separate explicit alternative.
placement_review.consumers: No production exact-ID or rival-bot ancestor consumers select these two composites. The existing broad objectives/impact/degrade consumer retains them. Three control scripts and one recorded expectation file now use the correct destination IDs.

controls: check.py exercises bound call targets, socketcall operation, syscall presence, architecture, code section, neutral packet generators, decoded suffix spacing, escape case, bounded proximity, split strings and missing hostile context. Existing Mirai controls cover preservation of split raw escaped arguments and original architectures.

validation.legacy_suite: testdata/triage/mirai-first-review/check.py fails mirai-name because loader-status-banner matches a bare MIRAI token. The identical failure was reproduced with a HEAD rules snapshot and original test expectations; unrelated to these changes.
